note: One entry per clip. 'segments' is the narration: one line per on-screen caption, in the order the captions appear in the scene.

segments.caption: A pretrained model only continues the text it is given.
segments.text: A pretrained model only continues the text it is given. We gave the base Smol L M two model the start of a discharge summary, and it simply kept going, repeating the same sentence about a myocardial infarction twice over. The model text in this clip is real output, not written for the slide.

segments.caption: Given a question, the base model repeats it instead of answering.
segments.text: Now we ask it a question about the note. The base model does not answer like an assistant. It just repeats the question back, because continuing text is all it was trained to do.

segments.caption: The post-trained model answers like an assistant, but here it is wrong.
segments.text: The post-trained version of the same model answers the question directly. But here its answer is wrong: the note says the patient denies chest pain. Clips three and four show two ways to fix this.

segments.caption: Post-training adds stages after pretraining.
segments.text: Post-training adds stages after pretraining: supervised fine-tuning, then preference tuning, then reinforcement learning with rewards that a program can check. We cover the last stage in clip four.

segments.caption: Supervised fine-tuning trains on instruction and answer pairs in a chat template.
segments.text: Supervised fine-tuning trains on instruction and answer pairs. Each pair is wrapped in a chat template, with special markers for where the user's turn and the assistant's turn begin and end.

segments.caption: The loss is the same next-token loss, counted only on the answer tokens.
segments.text: The loss is the same next-token loss as in pretraining. The only difference is that it is counted on the answer tokens, not on the instruction, so the model learns to write answers.

segments.caption: Same architecture and same loss: only the training data changes.
segments.text: So the architecture is the same and the loss is the same. Only the training data changes, from raw text to instruction and answer pairs, and that is what turns a text generator into an assistant.

segments.caption: Full fine-tuning with Adam stores about 16 bytes for every parameter.
segments.text: Full fine-tuning with the Adam optimizer stores about sixteen bytes for every parameter: the weight, its gradient, and two optimizer states. That is about five point eight gigabytes for this small model, and over a thousand for a seventy B model.

segments.caption: In SmolLM2-360M, one query projection W has 960 × 960 weights.
segments.text: Look at one weight matrix in Smol L M two: a query projection with nine hundred sixty rows and nine hundred sixty columns, about nine hundred twenty thousand weights. With Lora, it stays frozen.

segments.caption: LoRA adds two thin matrices, B and A, beside the frozen W.
segments.text: Lora adds two thin matrices beside it. A takes the token down to just eight numbers, and B brings it back up. The output is W times x, plus B times A times x.

segments.caption: B and A together have 15,360 weights, about 1.7% of W.
segments.text: B and A together have fifteen thousand, three hundred sixty weights. That is about one point seven percent of the frozen matrix, and only these are trained.

segments.caption: B starts at zero, so training starts exactly from the original model.
segments.text: B starts at zero, so at the first step B times A times x is zero, and the model gives exactly the original output. Training then moves only B and A.

segments.caption: Across all 32 layers, LoRA trains 1,638,400 weights, about 0.45% of the model.
segments.text: Add Lora to the query, key, value, and output projections in all thirty-two layers, and it trains one million, six hundred thirty-eight thousand, four hundred weights. That is about zero point four five percent of the model.

segments.caption: One frozen model can carry a small adapter for each clinical task.
segments.text: Because the base model never changes, one copy can serve many tasks. Each task, such as discharge summaries or radiology impressions, needs only its own small adapter, about three point three megabytes.

segments.caption: Preference data pairs one question with a chosen and a rejected answer.
segments.text: Preference data pairs one question with two answers. A clinician marks one as chosen and the other as rejected. Here the rejected answer gets the negation wrong.

segments.caption: Right now, SmolLM2-360M-Instruct rates the wrong answer as far more likely.
segments.text: Right now, Smol L M two rates the wrong answer as far more likely. Its log-probability is minus two point two four, while the correct answer gets minus twenty-one point zero nine.

segments.caption: RLHF trains a reward model on such choices, then reinforcement learning follows it.
segments.text: The classic method is R L H F. First, a separate reward model learns to score answers from many such choices. Then reinforcement learning, usually P P O, updates the language model to earn high scores. That means two models to train, and the training can be unstable.

segments.caption: DPO skips the reward model and compares the model with a frozen copy of itself.
segments.text: D P O skips the reward model. It keeps a frozen copy of the starting model, and for each answer it measures a gain: how much more likely the model in training makes that answer than the frozen copy does. The frozen copy keeps the model close to what it already knew.

segments.caption: The DPO loss gets smaller as the chosen gain pulls ahead of the rejected gain.
segments.text: The D P O loss takes the chosen gain minus the rejected gain, scales it by a small number called beta, here zero point one, and passes it through a sigmoid. The loss gets smaller as the chosen gain pulls ahead.

segments.caption: At the start, both gains are zero, so the loss is 0.69.
segments.text: At the start, the model is identical to its frozen copy, so both gains are zero. The sigmoid of zero is one half, and the loss is minus the log of one half, which is zero point six nine.

segments.caption: After training, the gains are +4 and −6, and the loss falls to 0.31.
segments.text: After some training, the chosen answer has gained four and the rejected answer has lost six. Beta times the gap of ten is one, the sigmoid of one is zero point seven three, and the loss falls to zero point three one.

segments.caption: A reasoning model writes out its thinking before it answers.
segments.text: A reasoning model writes out its thinking before it answers. For this E C G question, it reasons that S T elevation in leads two, three, and a V F points to the inferior wall, usually supplied by the right coronary artery, and answers B. The trace shown is illustrative.

segments.caption: DeepSeek-R1 learned this with rule-based rewards that a program can check.
segments.text: DeepSeek R one learned this with rewards that a simple program can check: one point if the final answer is correct, and one point if the reasoning sits inside the think tags. R one Zero used reinforcement learning alone. R one first saw a small set of long reasoning examples.

segments.caption: GRPO samples a group of answers to the same question and scores each one.
segments.text: The training method is called G R P O. For each question, the model writes a group of answers, and each one is scored. Here, only the first of four answers picks the right artery.

segments.caption: Each reward is compared with its own group: (reward − mean) ÷ std.
segments.text: Each reward is compared with its own group. The mean reward is zero point two five, and the standard deviation is zero point four three three. So the correct answer scores plus one point seven three, and each wrong answer scores minus zero point five eight. No separate critic model is needed.

segments.caption: Answers above their group's average become more likely, the others less likely.
segments.text: The model is then updated so that answers above their group's average become more likely, and answers below it become less likely. Over many questions, reasoning that reaches correct answers is reinforced.

segments.caption: A prompt can buy more tokens at test time, but not the ability to reason.
segments.text: Test time is different. Asked directly, Smol L M two gets the chest pain question wrong in nine tokens. Asked to reason first, it spends all six hundred tokens looping through twenty-eight numbered steps and never reaches an answer. The cost arrives, the benefit does not. Reasoning is something a model is trained to do, not something a prompt adds. Both are real output from the model.

segments.caption: Med-PaLM 2 samples several reasoning paths, then refines them into one answer.
segments.text: Med Palm two samples several reasoning paths for a medical question, then reads them all to write one refined answer. Together with a stronger base model and medical fine-tuning, this raised Med Q A accuracy from sixty-seven point two to eighty-six point five percent.

segments.caption: A fluent explanation is not proof: the rationale need not even match the answer.
segments.text: And a fluent explanation is not proof. On the E C G question, the same model answers D, the left main, which is wrong. Asked to reason, it invents a finding that was never in the question, argues its way to the left anterior descending, and then answers D anyway. The rationale does not even agree with the letter beside it. We return to checking reasoning in week twelve.
